title: Cadaveric Testing
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. The detector over collects on purpose: mark anything that is teaching rather than clinical direction as NOT_CLINICAL rather than deleting it.

positions.as_written: Read a sectioning result as what a structure restrains, not as how much a patient will feel.
Expect the magnitude of a cadaveric laxity change to exceed what examination finds in a patient, because muscle is absent.
State the loading condition alongside any cadaveric figure, since the figure is specific to it.
Check specimen number and whether the design was paired before weighing a cadaveric finding.
Ask whether sectioning order was randomised in a sequential study.
Treat reported precision as a property of the rig rather than of the knee.
Treat a cadaveric result as mechanism where a clinical study exists on the same question.
State that the bench to patient gap is argued rather than quantified.
Avoid giving a patient a cadaveric displacement as a prediction of their own knee.

Weigh the patient's age and physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations when deciding how much of this evidence to put into a conversation, because a specimen has none of them and the person in front of you is made of them.
